html:
The Bhopal disaster was a gas leak at a pesticide plant in Bhopal, central India, on the night of 2 to 3 December 1984. It is considered the world's worst industrial disaster.

About 40 tonnes of methyl isocyanate, a highly toxic gas, escaped from a tank at the Union Carbide India plant and drifted over the crowded slums around it while people slept. More than half a million people were exposed. The official count of immediate deaths is 2,259; other estimates put the deaths from the gas at 8,000 or more, and hundreds of thousands were injured, many for life.

The plant made pesticides for the farm boom of the Green Revolution. It was majority owned by the American firm Union Carbide. Investigations found safety systems switched off or broken and staff cut back before the leak.

The aftermath:

  • In 1989 Union Carbide paid 470 million US dollars in a settlement many victims called far too small.
  • Its chairman, Warren Anderson, was charged in India but never stood trial.
  • Dow Chemical bought Union Carbide in 2001 and says it has no liability.
  • The site was never fully cleaned up, and chemicals have leaked into the groundwater.

Bhopal belongs with Minamata and Chernobyl among the industrial disasters that changed how the world thinks about corporate responsibility and the risks poor neighbourhoods carry.
sum: The Bhopal disaster was a gas leak at a pesticide plant in Bhopal, central India, on the night of 2 to 3 December 1984. It is considered the world's worst industrial disaster.
